one_liner: GitHub offers a broad free REST (and GraphQL) API with self-serve OAuth apps and PATs, plus an official MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth apps support authorization-code and device flows, and anyone can register one self-serve. Personal access tokens are also supported. GitHub Apps authenticate with a JWT you mint yourself, which falls under OTHER. Basic auth with a password is retired for the public API.
access_notes: A free GitHub account gives working tokens. The API is not billed separately, and the rate limit is 5,000 requests per hour when authenticated. The partner programs on the fetched pages are optional and are not needed for API access. The Developer Program is open to individual developers.
blocker_notes: Nothing blocks a build. Some features, such as Copilot, need paid plans, but that falls on end customers. Partner programs are optional.

evidence.quote: You can create a personal access token, generate a token with a GitHub App, or use the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` in a GitHub Actions workflow.
GitHub's OAuth implementation supports the standard [authorization code grant type](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-4.1) and the OAuth 2.0 [Device Authorization Grant]
Every registered OAuth app is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret.
You must authenticate as a GitHub App in order to make REST API requests as the application.
The REST API is included with GitHub accounts; GitHub plans start at Free ($0/month), Team ($4/user/month), and Enterprise (from $21/user/month), but the API is not billed separately.
All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
